title: The impact of the acoustic environment on human emotion and experience: A case study of worship spaces
research_question: Does the acoustic environment enhance the emotional impact considering the match between acoustic and visual features of the built environment? Does the intensity of the emotional impact vary based on different acoustic environments? Does the intensity of the emotional impact differ based on the cultural background and familiarity of the sound (chant) and acoustic environment?

participants.description: 20 participants (9 males, 11 females) from diverse cultural backgrounds (religious affiliation, nationalities, etc.) with an average age of 29 (SD=4.9; Min=20; Max=40). All reported normal hearing.
participants.recruitment: Not explicitly stated, but study was approved by authors' institution Review Board.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Eight virtual reality scenes, each combining 3D binaural audio and 360° visuals of four worship spaces (two mosques, two churches). For each building, there was a 'dry' recording (sound without acoustic environment effect) and a 'wet' recording (sound with acoustic environment effect). Audio content was Quran recitations for mosques and Christian hymns for churches. Visuals were identical for dry and wet recordings of the same building.

measures.instrument: Five-point ordinal-category scale (1. None to 5. Highly)
Five-point ordinal-category scale (1. None to 5. Highly)
Keyword selection from a list (sad, tense, nostalgic, spiritual, inspired, cheerful, thrilled)

measures.construct: Familiarity with recording content (Islamic recitation, Christian hymns)
measures.instrument: Three-point scale (1. Not familiar, 2. Familiar, 3. Very familiar)
Four-point scale (1. Never, 2. Rarely, 3. Occasionally, 4. Frequently)

findings.mechanism: The sound felt more holy and sacred. Nostalgic. Reminded me of my own church experience. It was holy because of the ambiance and echoing by the wall.
findings.quote: The majority of participants described their experience with the wet recording as more calming and spiritual, and in many cases, nostalgic

mechanisms: The acoustic characteristics of the space can increase the intensity of the emotional impact and enhance the listener's experience considering audiovisual congruency.
Increase in heart rate and electrodermal activity is an indicator of an increase in emotional arousal.
Changes in the tonic level of EDR are an indicator of strong emotional response regardless whether it was positive or negative.
Self-report is a post-performance evaluation, while the physiological measurement (HRR/EDR) is considered a continuous (time-dependent) response.
High familiarity increases the intensity of the emotional impact based on the participants' self-report.
High physiological response could be a result of high arousal emotions other than the spiritual emotions mentioned above, such as excitement caused by surprise or unfamiliarity.

The pattern of physiological response represents the emotional response that results from the musical characteristics of the chant, and the difference in the response level represents the intensity of the emotional impact, which is higher with the wet recordings.
Sound reflections in the wet recording made the chant seem more harmonized.
The echo made the space feel spacious, and described the experience as immersive, providing a sense of belonging and inviting to participate.
implementation_implications: Demonstrated the importance of considering audiovisual congruency during the design process to enhance emotional impact.
Considering architectural features that contribute to creating similar acoustic characteristics in designing spaces where the cultural aspect plays an important role is essential.
Findings will help architects design better spaces in which acoustics are essential to the experience, such as worship spaces, performance spaces, meditative spaces, and museums.
The developed method can be used to assess the potential emotional impact of acoustic environments.
Visual and aural documentation and playback methods can be used to design multisensory VR representations in museums since acoustic heritage is an integral component of cultural heritage.

limitations: Binaural recordings did not account for head movement.

While visuals were held constant for dry/wet comparisons to control variables, the visuals did not match the dry recordings, which could impact the comparison of emotional impact between dry and wet recordings.
Generalizability of findings is limited to worship spaces; further research is needed for other building types.
Physiological measurements can be complicated to analyze due to potential effects of other factors unrelated to the stimulus.

paper_metadata.title: The impact of the acoustic environment on human emotion and experience: A case study of worship spaces
paper_metadata.crossref_title: The impact of the acoustic environment on human emotion and experience: A case study of worship spaces
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: People’s interactions with the environment shape their experiences. Thus, understanding these interactions is critical to enhancing human well-being. Aural attributes play a significant role in shaping the perception of space in addition to visual attributes. It is well known that sounds evoke an emotional response, but less is known about how the acoustic characteristics of environments reinforce such an emotional impact. By adopting virtual reality as a platform for recreating 3D sounds and 360° visuals of built environments of worship spaces as case studies, this study aims to investigate the influence of the acoustic environment considering audiovisual congruency on enhancing the human experience through self-report and physiological response analysis. It also examines the role of cultural background in terms of familiarity with the acoustic environment. The convergent mixed-methods approach, merging both quantitative and qualitative analysis, provides a deep understanding of the role of the acoustic environment in enhancing the auditory experience. The results show that the acoustic environment and audiovisual congruency amplify the intensity of the emotional impact, and the amplification of the impact can vary depending on the acoustic environment of the building. They also reveal that familiarity with sound and acoustic characteristics can increase this impact.
